test_cases.question: What does it mean for a supervisory authority to act with 'complete independence'?
test_cases.answer: Each supervisory authority shall act with complete independence in performing its tasks and exercising its powers. The member or members shall remain free from external influence, whether direct or indirect, and shall neither seek nor take instructions from anybody. They must also refrain from any action incompatible with their duties.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Each supervisory authority shall act with complete independence in performing its tasks and exercising its powers in accordance with this Regulation. The member or members of each supervisory authority shall, in the performance of their tasks and exercise of their powers in accordance with this Regulation, remain free from external influence, whether direct or indirect, and shall neither seek nor take instructions from anybody

test_cases.question: Are supervisory authority members allowed to hold other jobs while serving their term?
test_cases.answer: No. Members must not, during their term of office, engage in any incompatible occupation, whether gainful or not. They must also refrain from any action incompatible with their duties throughout their term.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Member or members of each supervisory authority shall refrain from any action incompatible with their duties and shall not, during their term of office, engage in any incompatible occupation, whether gainful or not

test_cases.question: What resources must Member States provide to supervisory authorities?
test_cases.answer: Each Member State must ensure that each supervisory authority is provided with the human, technical, and financial resources, premises, and infrastructure necessary for the effective performance of its tasks and exercise of its powers. This includes resources for mutual assistance, cooperation, and participation in the Board (EDPB).
test_cases.supporting_quote: Each Member State shall ensure that each supervisory authority is provided with the human, technical and financial resources, premises and infrastructure necessary for the effective performance of its tasks and exercise of its powers, including those to be carried out in the context of mutual assistance, cooperation and participation in the Board

test_cases.question: Who controls the staff of a supervisory authority?
test_cases.answer: Each Member State must ensure that each supervisory authority chooses and has its own staff. This staff shall be subject to the exclusive direction of the member or members of the supervisory authority concerned - not any external government ministry or body.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Each Member State shall ensure that each supervisory authority chooses and has its own staff which shall be subject to the exclusive direction of the member or members of the supervisory authority concerned
key_phrases: chooses and has its own staff

test_cases.question: What financial safeguards must Member States implement to protect supervisory authority independence?
test_cases.answer: Member States must ensure supervisory authorities are subject to financial control which does not affect their independence. Each SA must have separate, public annual budgets, which may be part of the overall state or national budget.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Each Member State shall ensure that each supervisory authority is subject to financial control which does not affect its independence and that it has separate, public annual budgets, which may be part of the overall state or national budget

b2b_relevance: MEDIUM - Article 52 establishes SA independence, which matters because: (1) SAs cannot be influenced by governments or industry to favor particular outcomes, (2) Decisions must be based on GDPR, not politics, (3) When dealing with an SA, understand they are truly independent regulators. Key takeaways: SA cannot take instructions from anyone - not government, not industry.
